status: Frozen independent native and phone findings for four requested candidates; not owner approval
independence: Read frozen production briefs and inspected the requested actual natives/repaired gear/WC Senn plus actual phone captures. Did not read lead-native-observations or independent reviewer verdicts. Author of initial concepts, not a blind design-author assessment.

observations.face_and_silhouette: Neris has a recognizable dark loose knot, heavy-lidded composed expression, teal/ivory masses and a dominant crescent shield. Portrait and full figure agree. The actual body is a narrow-waisted long-legged fashion athlete rather than the broader defender build in the concept; mature attractiveness is retained, but body-type differentiation is less strong than costume/weapon differentiation.
observations.gear_and_contact: Stillwall preserves G01-R1 solid crescent, pale rim, rear frame and actual fist/forearm attachment. The gloved fist wraps a real rear grip and cuff remains attached to the forearm; free hand is empty. Complete shield endpoints and boots are visible. No hard contact defect observed.
observations.linked_consistency: New character corresponds to frozen hair/costume/weapon directions with modest longer tunic tails. The repaired gear’s functional topology survives the character composition.
observations.texture: Face, skin, ivory shoulders and shield use broad values with little surface grain. Background paving is still densely mottled and wet, with many tiny reflected flecks and stone marks. Several bright vertical reflections compete with the legs. Hair has intentional strand grouping rather than pervasive microtexture.
observations.phone: Face and crescent identity remain distinct at 360px art width. Rear grip is too small to certify from phone alone, while the wet ground still creates high-frequency visual activity.
observations.assessment: Useful linked identity/gear candidate; no hard mechanical repair recommended in this bounded review. Texture goal only partly met.

observations.face_and_silhouette: Kellan reads as a new youthful adult fighter through clustered black curls, tooth-showing grin, sand double-breasted jacket and cobalt insert. His crouched turn differs from the two women. Face vocabulary remains conventionally narrow-jawed and handsome; costume/hair/stance do more differentiation than radically different facial construction.
observations.gear_and_contact: Both bare hands visibly wrap the actual Winterline hilt on the same side of the oval guard. Blade is single, connected and clear of body; full tip, pommel and both boots remain within frame. Shape/ivory edge correspond to G02-R1 with perspective taper. No hand wraps the sharp blade.
observations.linked_consistency: Frozen black curls, sand/cobalt costume, dark tapered trousers and pale boots preserved. Weapon remains recognizable as the repaired source.
observations.texture: Clean jacket and face planes, simple blade reflection and sparse distant lights are much calmer than original WC character rendering. Wet paving still carries numerous irregular small highlights/cracks. Background is nearly the same moonlit reservoir grammar as C01, reducing setting variety between these boards.
observations.phone: Teeth-showing grin, light jacket, stance and long sword read readily. Fine grip verification still relies on native. Paving creates residual busy contrast without obscuring the person.
observations.assessment: No hard anatomical, grip or framing failure observed. Better subject-surface simplicity; background noise remains.

observations.face_and_silhouette: Elowen’s long strawberry braid, freckles, stern alert expression and slate/ivory archer silhouette are distinguishable from Neris’s dark knot and relaxed shield stance. Portrait/full body agree. Body is tall and slender as planned. Freckles are denser than the few marks requested but are an identity feature, not a complexion score.
observations.gear_and_contact: One hand wraps the real Daystring center grip. One continuous undrawn string connects the two smooth green tips, with ordinary body occlusion where it passes the arm; free hand is empty, no arrow or spare string. Bow endpoints and boots fully visible. G03-R1 geometry survives the rendering change from Sunbreak gear to Nightglass character.
observations.linked_consistency: Braid, hip coat, ivory chest shell, gloves and bow are retained. Hand-at-hip becomes a relaxed lowered free hand, a harmless pose change.
observations.texture: Broad foreground paving, calmer water reflection and larger distant cliff masses are quieter than C01/C02. Face and coat avoid grain. Hair still has many strands and portrait freckles add local detail, but they do not spread across every material.
observations.phone: Hair color/braid, expression, ivory chest and bow distinguish the character immediately. Undrawn string is thin but main bow silhouette remains clean.
observations.assessment: Best balance of clean subject surfaces and quiet setting among these three in this reviewer’s judgment; no hard functional repair identified.

observations.face_and_silhouette: Senn retains WC C02 chestnut high ponytail, muscular bare arms, navy long vest, ivory breastplate and distinctive lance. Her focused open-mouth exertion is appropriate to a new airborne counter. Two arms and two legs remain coherent and the entire adult is framed.
observations.gear_and_contact: Both hands visibly wrap separated portions of one continuous Crownfall shaft; full butt and spearhead are framed. Tip has an explicit air gap before the toad head, matching the frozen pre-contact beat. No false impact spark. Water blast passes beneath her body, with separation from both legs.
observations.linked_consistency: The liked WC adult and weapon remain recognizable rather than an anchor substitution. Armor carries some inherited facets. Toad is one broad amphibian; two foreground forelegs read, while hindquarters extend beyond/behind the right edge, so four-limb topology cannot be fully certified from this scene alone.
observations.action_and_causality: Open mouth is clearly the source of ONE broad connected jet; its direction is right-to-left under Senn. Her spear counter points toward the head and her launch shelf is visible at left. Foreground dry rock can serve as a later landing surface, but the precise touchdown trajectory is less explicit than source/blast/evasion. This is a decisive active combat beat rather than another ready stance.
observations.texture: Big dam, cliff and creature masses establish clear hierarchy and stronger daylight range. However, white foam lace, mottled toad skin, flecked foreground rocks and stippled treelines are conspicuous fine detail. It succeeds in action staging more clearly than in the strict broad-surface/no-pervasive-texture goal.
observations.phone: Mouth-to-jet causal chain, airborne Senn and countering spear remain immediately legible. Foam collapses into a bright broad shape at small size, but remains visually active; native is needed for grip, air gap and anatomy.
observations.assessment: No hard action/contact failure identified for the explicitly pre-contact beat. Retain caveats about residual texture, cropped hindquarter anatomy and less explicit landing destination.

summary.main_remaining_issue: Texture simplification is uneven: clean faces/costume/gear largely succeed, but C01/C02 wet paving and S04 foam/skin/rock details retain significant fine visual activity. This is a material goal limitation, not a reason to invent anatomy defects.
summary.differentiation: Hair, expression, costume blocks, pose and weapon distinguish all three new adults; bodies/facial proportions remain comparatively conventional and slender.
summary.scope_limit: This bounded review does not approve unseen new scenes/abilities or the overall proof gate, infer owner preferences, certify obscured toad hind limbs, or promise repeated motion continuity.
